title: Sachertorte
description: A dense chocolate cake split and sealed with apricot jam, then poured over with a mirror glaze. Baked in a 23 cm springform and cut small, because it is very rich. Whipped cream on the side is not optional in Vienna.
notes: Three separate operations that each want your full attention — cake, jam seal, glaze. Bake a day ahead if you can; the crumb firms up overnight and slices far more cleanly.

steps.text: Melt the dark chocolate over a pan of steaming water and leave it to come down to barely warm.
steps.tip: Hot chocolate meeting soft butter seizes it into grains. Blood heat on the inside of your wrist is the test.

steps.text: Beat the butter with the icing sugar and the vanilla extract until pale, then beat in the egg yolks one at a time.
Fold the cooled chocolate through the butter mixture.
Whip the egg whites with the salt to soft peaks, then rain in the caster sugar and whip to a meringue that flops over at the tip.
steps.tip: Stiff peaks tear rather than fold, and every tear is a streak of dry white in the finished crumb.

steps.text: Slacken the batter with a third of the meringue, then alternate the rest of the meringue with the sifted plain flour in three additions.
Bake in a lined 23 cm springform until a skewer comes out with a few damp crumbs clinging to it.
Cool in the tin for ten minutes, then turn out onto a rack and leave until stone cold.
Slice the cold cake horizontally into two even layers.
Warm the apricot jam with the rum until it pours, then push it through a sieve to catch the fruit pieces.
Spread half the jam over the cut face, sandwich the cake back together, and paint the rest thinly over the top and sides. Leave it to set to a tacky film.
steps.tip: The jam is not a filling, it is a seal. Skip it and the glaze drags loose crumb around with it as it runs.

steps.text: Boil the caster sugar with the water to a light syrup.
Off the heat, stir the chopped dark chocolate into the syrup and let it cool until it ribbons off the spoon and coats the back of it.
steps.tip: Too hot and it runs off in a thin veil; too cool and it sets before it has covered the sides.

steps.text: Stand the cake on a rack over a tray and pour the glaze onto the centre in one continuous movement, letting it find its own way down.
steps.tip: Never touch it with a palette knife. Every mark you make in a poured glaze is permanent.

steps.text: Leave to set at room temperature — the fridge kills the shine.
